title: Linux Foundation Launches OpenGrid to Build Open, Shared Infrastructure for Electric Grid
source_used: Linux Foundation press release (linuxfoundation.org), read directly via the Google News link
key_facts: The Linux Foundation, a nonprofit organisation that hosts open-source software projects, announced the launch of OpenGrid on 7 Oct 2026 at Open Source Summit Europe in Prague.
OpenGrid is a shared data and interoperability layer that lets existing commercial and open-source grid planning tools work together; it is not a replacement for them.
It will provide open standards and schemas, programmatic APIs and a central Data Hub for validated, model-ready datasets.
Its first application, the OpenGrid Translator, is in development for release in 2027 and will move data and models between commercial platforms and open-source tools.

The release says more than 2,500 gigawatts of generation, storage and large-load projects are pending in grid connection queues worldwide; annual grid investment needs to roughly double to more than $600 billion by 2030.
The release says 80 million kilometres of power lines must be added or replaced by 2040.
OpenGrid launches with support from Breakthrough Energy GRIDS, Global Grid Catalyst, Connected Grid Initiative and Google.org.
Jim Zemlin is CEO of the Linux Foundation; Alice Yake is vice president of Breakthrough Energy GRIDS and chair of the OpenGrid Management Committee.
quote_evidence: Grid planning has become a critical bottleneck as electricity demand grows, new data center and industrial loads come online and more generation and storage seek connection.
OpenGrid is not developing a single replacement for existing grid planning software.
Today, too many plans rely on data others cannot verify and tools much of the world cannot afford,
why_it_matters_hint: Open-source planning tools for utilities and regulators, as data centres add to grid demand; no results yet, first tool due 2027.
event_date: 7 Oct 2026 (launch at Open Source Summit Europe, Prague)
notes: Primary source read directly: the Linux Foundation release. The pool item (HPCwire) is an off-the-wire copy of this release, so the source is the Linux Foundation.
